Why this database first: If you only run one resonance database regularly, make it the Schuessler Salts (minerals). Minerals are the building blocks of the body, and this database works on that foundation level: physical, emotional and energetic at once.

A house is not stable without foundations. In the Schuessler tradition the mineral cell salts are the body's foundations. When they are strong, we are less likely to 'take things on', whether stress, other people's energy or the pressures of a demanding season of life.
That is why it is the database to work with on a daily basis, and the one to return to when something in life feels like it is missing its foundation.
What it is: Schuessler salts are 12 basic mineral 'cell salts' (also called tissue salts) named after Dr. Wilhelm Heinrich Schüssler (1821-1898), a German doctor in Oldenburg. They are minerals found naturally in the tissues of the human body, prepared in a low-potency, homeopathic-style dilution.
Origins: Schüssler published his findings in a German homeopathic journal in March 1873, influenced by the Dutch physiologist Jacob Moleschott's work on minerals in the body.
Simplicity: he narrowed the thousands of homeopathic remedies of his day to 12 core minerals, which makes the system far easier to learn and use.
27 salts today: his students later added 15 'additional' salts (No. 13-27); the 12 basic salts remain the foundation and the additional salts serve special purposes.
Widely used: spread quickly to the English-speaking world and still a staple in Germany, where the salts are known simply by number.
The foundation principle: Schüssler's core idea: when the body's mineral balance is off, the body cannot function at its best. Everything else is built on top of that foundation.
The etheric body: I use the mineral cell salts for the etheric body. They are the building blocks, the full foundation of everything else we work on.
Modern life drains it: with today's reliance on highly processed foods, keeping a healthy mineral balance is often difficult.
It works on many levels: the foundation is physical, but it also shapes protection, resilience and how connected we are to ourselves.
Daily practice: because it is foundational, it is worth working with the cell salts every day if you possibly can.
What makes this Healy database different: Most databases give you a name and a frequency. The Schuessler Salts resonance analysis gives a full picture for each mineral that comes up (purple resonance section of the Healy app).
Present state: the emotional symptoms you may notice when this mineral is low.
Desired state: the quality the mineral supports when in balance.
Body field: where in the body the information is directed.

Key point: it is not only the mineral that is vibrated into your information field; the desired-state description is sent too. Think of it as working with what the mineral represents, not just the mineral itself.

What it is: The I Ching, or Book of Changes, is one of the oldest texts in the world. It began as a divination manual in China's Western Zhou period (around 1000-750 BC), so it carries roughly 3,000 years of wisdom. Traditionally consulted by casting yarrow stalks or tossing coins, which produce one of 64 hexagrams: six stacked lines, each solid (yang) or broken (yin).

Core teaching: everything changes, like water in a river. Our task is not to force change into the shape we want, but to understand what a moment is asking of us and grow with it. Life moves in cycles; some call for withdrawing and going within, others for action. We struggle when we push against the cycle we are actually in.

Two building blocks: yang (active, driving energy) and yin (receptive, nurturing energy). Combined in different patterns they describe every state of change: physical, emotional, mental and spiritual. In 1679 Leibniz drew on the same on/off pattern for the binary system that runs every computer.
Why it belongs on the Healy: It is built into the Resonance analysis: the I Ching analysis scans your energy field against your focus and returns the top hexagrams for that moment, which you can then send as frequencies.

It works through synchronicity: like a coin toss, the result reflects the quality of the present moment. It externalises what you already know within but cannot yet see (C. G. Jung described the hexagram as an expression of the moment in which it was cast).

It is inspired by nature: its images come from natural processes (water, mountains, wind, thunder), which sits naturally beside a frequency-based approach to balance. Many practitioners feel its view of a connected, ever-changing world echoes how modern physics describes reality.

It links with Human Design: the 64 hexagrams correspond to the 64 gates, and the six hexagram lines map onto the six line profiles (Investigator, Hermit, Martyr/Experimenter, Opportunist, Heretic, Role Model). If you or your clients use Human Design, the scan adds another layer.
Why use it: 1. Clarity at a crossroads: When a big life, work or relationship decision is waiting, it gives you a lens on what this moment needs.
Why use it: 2. Harmony in relationships: It brings the dynamics with partners and family into awareness, so you can see a situation from another perspective.
Why use it: 3. Shows the effects of your: It points to where a path is likely to lead and helps you shape a strategy to reach your goals.
Why use it: 4. Reassures or challenges,: Each hexagram shows both sides of the coin: the encouragement and the thing you still need to work on.
Why use it: 5. Deepens your spiritual pr: It brings an ancient philosophy of change into everyday life and decisions.
Why use it: 6. A ready-made coaching ses: Set a focus, scan, read the results together and let the client find their own meaning. It can fill a whole session.
Why use it: 7. Timing in business: It can tell you whether this is a time to build quietly and work things out, or to get out, network and be seen.
Why use it: 8. Awareness plus frequency: When you understand the message, you bring the healing into conscious awareness and relate far more to the frequencies you are sending.

A session, step by step: 1. Set one clear focus. Without a focus, the scan becomes a melting pot of everything going on in someone's life. Other themes (such as family) may still show up if they affect the focus.
2. Tune in and scan. Take a few breaths, have the client hold their focus and feeling, then run the I Ching analysis.
3. Write down the numbers. Note every hexagram in order.
4. Look each one up. Start with the reading at a glance or your quick-meaning sheet.
5. Turn it into a question. For each hexagram ask: what is this asking of me right now? Look for themes that repeat across results.
6. Let the client interpret. Offer insights, but the meaning is theirs; it works a little like an oracle card reading.
7. Send the frequencies, now with conscious awareness behind them.
8. Follow up. Send the links for each hexagram, or a short summary of the key messages and reflection questions. Avoid long, dense PDFs: they can overwhelm.

When to use it: 1. Before and after a Healy program or a meditation: the classic use. The aura-cleanse meditation fits as the 'middle' step: scan, meditate and vibrate, then scan again.
2. Morning and evening: scan in the morning, run a program or vibrate, then scan again before bed. Write the results down, because patterns matter more than single readings.
3. At the start of a client or coaching session, before you set the focus, so the focus comes from what is actually showing up.

4. During a transition: a breakup, a move, a business launch or a 'no man's land' phase. Your spiritual-transformation session matches chakra themes to programs like Being, Release, Coherence and Inner Strength.
5. Before business decisions: scan the 'aura of your business vision' with a clarity focus, as in the business energetics session.
6. At distance, with permission. Always get permission before using the Healy on someone, and start gently.
Best practices from your sessions: Scan first, then add the focus. The first aura scan has no focus; you add the focus afterwards for the deeper analysis.
Don't tune in before the baseline scan if you want an honest 'before'. Guiding the group to tune in first pushed the scores up.
High doesn't mean balanced. A very high score can mean chaos or overcompensation, like over-giving in the heart. Look at which chakras change between scans, not just the lowest three.
Select all seven chakras with one result each. Results don't come back in low-to-high order, and the chakras affect each other.
Take several scans and look for what repeats. Things that appear consistently are usually yours; things that disappear may have been picked up from others.
Read the colour notes. For example, 'root shining in sacral orange' can be read as one chakra compensating for another. Visualise the correct colour back in its own chakra while you vibrate.
Ground it with a real step. After the scan, choose one physical action towards the focus.
Don't overdo frequency use. Healy's own app manual advises avoiding extremes and not going over two to three frequency applications a day.
Framing for clients: Present the aura scan as a reflective, intuitive tool and not a diagnostic reading. Your own teaching already frames it this way: use the scan to tune in, notice and choose a focus. That is the most defensible framing if a client asks.

What it is: The Coaching module sits in the HealAdvisor Analyze ('blue dot') app alongside the Resonance and Aura analyses. It names specific life areas and sub-areas and works around a focus you write yourself.
Results show only the desired state, so the client reads (ideally out loud) what they are growing towards.
Why use it: It's more specific than the: 1. It gives answers about your life, not just your energy. The Aura scan reads things at an energetic level in the body; Coaching names specific life areas (finances, self-worth, goals, relationships), so the results are easier to act on.

2. You can drill into sub-categories. Clicking the arrow on a category opens its sub-areas, for example 'Finding a partner' or 'Trust' inside Personal Relationships, and 'Boundaries' or 'Dissolve imprints and ancestral claims' inside Family. You can scan the whole category or narrow it right down.
3. You choose how many readings you get. The Aura scan gives a fixed three per chakra. In Coaching you set the number per category (up to about 20), so you decide where to go deep.
Why use it: It works around your own foc: 4. You write the focus yourself. The client's own affirmation, in their own words and in the present tense, becomes the lens for the whole scan. That keeps it personal and aimed at what they want.

5. It turns insight into an action plan. Most people get a Human Design or Gateways to Gold report and then don't know what to do with it. You can put the healing affirmation from a gate (for example Gate 44, 'I see the pattern and I choose a new path...') into the focus and work on it directly.
6. You can follow on from a One scan result. Take the affirmation that resonated most and put it into Coaching to go a level deeper, as in the business energetics step.
Why use it: It shows what's really going: 7. It often shows the real issue is somewhere else. In Ali's session the scan started on finances and ended in Potentials, with 'I am active and organized.' Underneath was guilt about time away from the kids. The answer is often in a different category from where you started.
8. It works like peeling an onion. You start with the symptoms and follow each result into the next scan, from order and time, to self-worth, to the fear underneath.
9. It shows the source of stress. In the vagus nerve example, finances and goals came up as the life areas tied to the imbalance. It shows where life is out of balance, not just that it is.
10. Green results are useful too. A green category shows where the focus is already working. That is a strength to build on, so you don't have to pick only the red ones.
11. It shows how deep something sits. In Coaching, D and C are cause and effect and easier to shift. LM is background and harder to change. That helps you decide what to work on first.
12. The negative relevances show deep material. Results with negative percentages point to themes held deep in the subconscious, like the ancestral imprints that came up in the Gate 44 demo.
Why use it: It works well in a coaching: 13. The scan prompts the client's own insights. Ali reached her own breakthroughs from the results without being told what they meant. The coach holds the space and the scan opens the conversation.
14. It pairs naturally with the Wheel of Life. The eight-area wheel exercise feeds straight into choosing categories and a focus.
15. Turning on every category gives you a full wheel of life. It takes away the 'which one do I pick?' problem. Just read the top six to eight results.
16. You get desired-state affirmations, not negatives. The results only show the desired state, so the client reads (ideally out loud) what they're growing towards.
17. It works for groups. One shared focus scanned for the room, like the group's finance pattern, gives a collective experience.
18. It's flexible to deliver. You can send it after the session while the client journals or rests, or for three days in a row at an agreed time. Short sessions work too ('less is more').
19. It combines with your other tools. Use it after an Aura scan, with the MagHealy vagus nerve program, or alongside the Bach flower and creative homeopathy scans.
Why use it (from the web: general coachi: 20. It makes vague imbalance visible. Many coaching conversations begin with clients feeling something in their lives is out of balance but not being able to identify which areas need attention. A life-area map solves that.
21. It sets priorities. The Wheel of Life can be used by anyone with little or no training, but is commonly completed in coaching sessions to identify and agree priorities for future exploration.
22. It shows strengths as well as gaps: which areas of your life are strongest and which need most attention (same idea as looking at the green categories).

23. Goals the client chooses work better. Research found goals initiated by the client rather than the coach were positively related to successful coaching outcomes, a strong reason to have clients write their own focus.

24. It's worth repeating over time. Life-wheel tools recommend going back regularly to check your life direction and readjust, especially after drastic life events. Repeat scans with the same focus can track progress the same way.
25. One focus at a time works better. General coaching guidance says goals are not met if too much focus is placed in other areas; this matches your advice to pick one focus per scan.
Framing: Web sources are about coaching in general, so they back up the method, not the frequency side. If students repeat any of this to clients, keep it framed as a coaching and reflection tool rather than a health claim.

What it is: Across the sessions, the trainer treats the All Healy Programs scan as a triage scan: you use it to find which program groups matter before you look for individual programs.
Why start with it: 1. It tells you which: The Pink app has dozens of program groups, and you can't know in advance which one someone needs. This scan ranks the groups. In her demo, Gold Cycle came top at 62%, followed by Mental Balance, Watch Meridian, Skin and Power of Three.
Why start with it: 2. It's the first ste: You can't open specific programs from this overview. You go back to New Resonance Analysis and scan each top category on its own. For example, Power of Three gave Kapha and Rebalance, and Skin gave Skin Impurity Systemic at 60%.
Why start with it: 3. Her default for ph: Her default for physical concerns like body pain or health issues, and for when you have no idea where to start.
Why start with it: 4. The basis of a cli: In the stress/migraine case study, the overview pointed to Watch Meridian (gallbladder and stomach), Sleep (Bed Rest), Gold (Care and Relax), Fitness (Strength) and Crown Chakra. Those became the 14-day schedule.
Why start with it: 5. It shows which Pin: Shows which Pink program to run if you want to decode its frequencies. Bioenergetic Boost came top for her, so that is the one she ran and decoded.
How to read the percentages: The top result is the most relevant one. She treats anything above 50% as relevant.

Percentages are relative within each scan, not across scans. If Pure scores 50% inside Gold Cycle and Mental Balance Acute scores 60% in its own scan, that does not mean Mental Balance matters more. Follow the order from the overview, where Gold ranked first.
Step-by-step: 1. Set a focus or goal first, using a questionnaire or discovery call. Without a focus, you have nothing to measure results against.
2. In the Blue app, go to Resonance, then Healy Program Groups, then New Resonance Analysis. Choose the database All Healy Programs and start the analysis.
3. Take a photo of the results so you don't have to keep switching screens.
4. Scan each of the top categories separately.
5. Optionally scan 3 times (a tip from Jazz Deep). Results that keep coming back are the person's own; results that appear and disappear may be energy picked up from other people.
6. Build the list or schedule. Then run the programs in the Pink app or send them from Lists in the Blue app.
7. If the client doesn't own a module that comes up (Watch Meridian is common), use the closest program they do have, such as the Meridian programs.
Before the scan: The Pink and Blue apps can't both connect at once. If the Healy won't connect, swipe the other app closed and scan for the device again.
Reset by holding the middle button for 20-30 seconds until the light stays on (she does this weekly).

If you get the spinning sync wheel, switch to airplane mode or turn off automatic sync. You only need internet for cloud sync and database updates, but sync now and then so your databases stay current.
Have the client relaxed, breathing calmly and open. You can do the fingerprint for them. Don't talk while scanning; tune in instead.
Choosing databases by goal: Physical / body pain: All Healy Programs, Schuessler Salts, Materia Medica, Vital Substances, Digital Nutrition.
Mental / emotional: Schuessler Salts (connects emotion and body part), Bach Flowers, Australian Bush Flowers, Creative Homeopathy (takes about 10 minutes).
Energetic / protection: Alaskan Gem Elixirs, Australian Bush Flowers, Bach.
Direction, decisions, relationships, business: I Ching (scanning a relationship needs both people's consent).
Session limits and ending: Scan no more than about 5 databases per session, and up to 3 Pink programs. Focusing on a single database is often better, because clients get tired and overwhelmed.
End with Alaskan Gem Elixirs so the session finishes on a positive note.
Schuessler Salts (1) gives more detail than Schuessler Salts 2: it shows the present state, the desired state and the body area.
'Stimulation Programs' with Roman numerals are the Pain Psyche programs. If they come up, scan Pain Psyche to see the program names.
Vital Substances may not appear on some devices. Look at the very bottom of the database list.
Reading the results with a client: Let the client read the results first and ask what resonates. Then explain.
Lead with the desired state (the solution), then the present state (the problem). Make clear that what you send is the positive.
Have them read any affirmation aloud 3 times.
Don't go into potencies or percentages in a first session. If it helps, the short version is: D = physical, C = mental/emotional, LM = spiritual.
If something doesn't resonate, it may not be theirs, and it's still fine to release it.
Healy doesn't tell you whether something is needed physically (TimeWaver does). Use judgement; for example Vital Substances results can point to foods.
Reference materials: The Full Healy Resources folder is on the members-area Google Drive. Print the PDFs into a binder and search inside them with Ctrl+F. It includes: Alaskan Gem Elixirs (49), Australian Bush Flowers (negative and positive states, plus combinations), Bach Flowers (38 remedies, a page each), Creative Homeopathy (introduction only), Digital Nutrition table (English and German), Materia Medica appendix, Potency chart, Schuessler Salts (with links), Vital Substances table, I Ching meanings, Acute vs. chronic vs. systemic.

The Healy program descriptions PDF is worth sending to clients along with their results.

HealAdvisor Search lets you search a topic (e.g. 'broken bones') and add the suggested programs to a schedule. A later session notes it stopped giving ailment-specific programs (it now shows 'Burdens 1-4'), so check whether it currently works that way.
Keep records: your scans save to Lists, and a weekly spreadsheet shows patterns over time.
Decoding Pink frequencies: Watch the Hz values on the device and look them up one at a time. The middle of a program is the most relevant part, and percentages only start appearing about halfway through. A negative % means you're below the ideal for that frequency.
Caution (from your notes): AI tools like ChatGPT write a plausible explanation for any number you give them. Treat those answers as prompts for reflection, not established facts.
Sending frequencies afterwards: Go to Lists and send each scan. A few seconds (8-17) is enough to imprint, a minute is fine, and 2:50 per list is typical. For something chronic, send once or twice a day.
Compliance: The trainer stresses compliance: say Healy may 'rebalance', not 'heal'. Serious conditions still need medical care, so keep that framing with clients.
